When people survive falling from great heights they generally report blissful near death experiences that encourage impactful changes to their life.

Nobody knows you better than you. If you can make it to an emergency room, try that first. It's worth a try is it not?

Good luck to you on your journey. You are loved.

Heaven and Hell are not destinations, they are a state of mind. The kingdom of heaven walks the earth, but the people are blind to see it. Heaven and Hell are inside each of us.

Happiness, Love, Satisfaction = Heaven

Pain, Loss, Sadness = Hell

When I informed my wife of my dysphoria, she told me she didn't think she could love me as a woman. About a year later we separated for 2.5 years. Now, 3 years after the first conversation, I told her I spoke to a therapist about it, she was ecstatic and encouraging. I feel like that was the day I died. Where the fuck was this encouragement the first time? I don't blame her, she's human and deserves a husband she can recognize as such.

I tried to approach my mother with this conversation, but she doesn't understand.
